content.text:
I fixed it: the http adapter now lowercases the `content-encoding` header before deciding how to decompress. Values like `GZIP`, `Gzip` or `Br` are now treated the same as `gzip` and `br`, so responses like the storage.googleapis.com one in the issue get decompressed. I haven't run any tests.

The change is one line, the `switch` in `lib/adapters/http.js` at line 474:

```js
switch ((res.headers['content-encoding'] || '').toLowerCase()) {
```

The `|| ''` fallback covers HEAD and 204 responses. For those, the code just above deletes the header before the `switch` runs, so without the fallback `toLowerCase()` would be called on `undefined` and throw.
